subject: PayNet integration follow-up — tool definitions & parallel call approach

messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Jenkins <sam.jenkins@paynet.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayNet discovery recap: tool definitions, routing, and next steps

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single reference for the engineering team. Short version up front: Redwood recommends a tool-definition manifest + a hybrid parallel/sequential invocation strategy, OIDC short-lived tokens for auth (or API key for POC), region-aware routing with a cost-tier fallback, and an embedding+cross-encoder rerank for downstream accuracy.

Call highlights (from our notes):
- Primary integration surface: customer support triage (ticket enrichment) and automated billing assistant.
- Sensitive data: PII redaction requirement; PayNet needs audit logs and key rotation.
- SLA target: p95 < 350ms for interactive flows, batching allowed for async batch jobs.

Technical proposals (high level):
1) Tool definitions manifest (attached): canonical list of tools the model can call (name, input schema, side_effects boolean, idempotency_key rules, rate_limit). We attached paynet_tool_def_manifest_v1.yaml for you to review.
2) Parallel vs sequential: run read-only lookups (customer profile, product catalog, embeddings search) in parallel. Reserve sequential calls for side-effecting operations (refunds, status transitions) to avoid race conditions.
3) Auth: for long-term deployment we recommend OIDC short-lived tokens + mTLS for private deployment; for POC an API key scoped to routes is fine.
4) Routing + fallback: prefer region affinity -> model performance tier -> cost tier. Automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model if throughput constraints are hit.
5) Structured output / tools: return a JSON action envelope (action_name, args, confidence, provenance). Example schema is in the attached sample_prompts and manifest.
6) Embeddings & rerank: use vector search (FAISS or managed vector index) to shortlist from KB, then re-rank top N with a cross-encoder or a light-weight reranker to improve precision for action generation.

Next steps / asks from PayNet:
- Confirm priority: tool-calling (triage) vs pure NLU (intent/classification).
- Confirm auth preference (API key POC vs OIDC for pilot).
- Make engineering contact for a short scoping doc (we recommend 1-2 engineers + 1 security contact).

I've attached the initial tool manifest and a one-page auth flow diagram. If this looks good I can schedule a 30m architecture session next week with Rishi and Neha to walk through the manifest and sample SDK snippets.

Best,
Laura Bennett

Subject: Re: PayNet discovery recap: tool definitions, routing, and next steps

Thanks Laura — this is super helpful. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) Auth: Security prefers OIDC + mTLS for anything production, but we could do an API key for the POC if you recommend it. Is the SDK sample you mentioned supporting token exchange (OIDC) out of the box?
2) Fallback: if you fall back to a smaller model, do you preserve the same tool-defined action semantics? We need deterministic behavior for certain billing ops.
3) Rerank: curious about latency trade-offs for shortlist size. Our p95 target is strict.

If possible, please include a short SDK snippet showing the recommended call pattern (parallel lookups -> action generation -> guarded side-effect call) and an example of the JSON action envelope. Also cc'd Emily (CTO) to keep her in the loop on compliance requirements.

—Sam
Sam Jenkins
Head of Integrations, PayNet
